result.summary: Do not ship: password changes no longer revoke compromised sessions.

findings.title: Stolen session cookies retain access after password changes
findings.body: Changing only password_hash preserves the signing secret, so an attacker holding a pre-change triggarr_session cookie can still access protected routes after the owner changes their password. AuthMiddleware accepts that cookie at triggarr/web/middleware.py:145–148 without checking the password hash; validate_session in triggarr/auth.py checks only its signature and 30-day expiry. The removed rotation previously revoked these cookies immediately, and no replacement revocation check protects this path.
findings.recommendation: Restore atomic session-secret rotation with the password update and reissue the acting user's cookie under the new secret. Verify that another device's pre-change cookie is rejected.

next_steps: Restore revocation and run the existing password-change rotation, cookie-reissue, and other-device eviction tests in tests/test_auth_routes.py.
